title: JANUS Engine — Axle Faraday / transformer-analogy / generator-harvest analysis
question: Does the rotating magnetic Axle create a transformer-like electromagnetic effect and can useful electrical energy be collected into the startup/surplus battery?

answer.short: Yes, if magnetic flux changes through an intentionally wound stationary coil. That is generator action governed by Faraday induction. The existing coreless AFPM starter-generator is already the correct device to collect it.
answer.transformer_analogy: A transformer and a generator share Faraday's law. A transformer changes magnetic flux without mechanical rotation; JANUS changes flux at the stationary stator because the magnetic Axle rotates relative to it.
answer.mechanical_limit: P_electric_out <= tau_external * omega after conversion losses
answer.back_emf_relation: V_oc approximately proportional to omega for a frozen PM geometry: V_oc = k_e * omega

important_distinction.useful_generator_path: Axle PM field -> stationary AFPM windings -> bidirectional inverter/rectifier -> DC bus -> battery
important_distinction.bulk_copper_or_brass_path: time-varying field -> eddy currents inside the conductive Axle/chamber -> Lenz reaction torque + heat
important_distinction.interpretation: The second path is analogous to an unintended shorted transformer secondary. It is normally a parasitic loss, not an attractive power-harvesting route.

energy_boundary.battery_driven_spin: If the battery/AFPM motor is the only source spinning the Axle, simultaneously harvesting generator power from the same motion cannot create a net gain. Generator loading increases opposing torque and the motor must supply that energy plus losses.
real_regeneration: external water current drives or assists Axle rotation
a process pressure/flow source independently supplies shaft work
Axle is decelerating and finite rotational kinetic energy is being recovered
another independently identified mechanical source drives the shaft
energy_boundary.PEMFC_boundary: If PEMFC electricity drives the AFPM motor and the same motor-generator immediately regenerates from that self-created shaft motion, the loop is lossy and cannot add energy.

JANUS_control_opportunity.name: AUTO_MOTOR_TO_REGEN_CROSSOVER
JANUS_control_opportunity.principle: Use one bidirectional coreless AFPM machine. During startup it consumes battery power as a motor. If water/hydraulic torque later reduces required motor torque to zero and then exceeds process drag, the inverter automatically crosses into generator mode and charges the battery.
JANUS_control_opportunity.torque_balance: tau_hydraulic + tau_other_external - tau_process_drag - tau_bearing - tau_eddy = tau_generator
JANUS_control_opportunity.regeneration_condition: tau_external_available * omega > total mechanical losses and generator/inverter losses
JANUS_control_opportunity.benefit: No separate generator is required; the same magnetic hardware can start, hold RPM, brake regeneratively and recover genuine external mechanical surplus.

tests: open-circuit back-EMF versus RPM at 60/120/300/600 RPM
shaft torque increase when electrical load is applied
motor efficiency and inverter bidirectional efficiency
battery charge power when independently spinning the Axle
motor-current reduction when hydraulic flow assists the Axle
zero-current crossover where hydraulic torque exactly carries rotational demand
regenerative region where DC-bus power reverses into the battery
simultaneous B(theta,t), RPM, torque, bus current and temperature logging
controls: coils connected to resistive/dummy electrical load
battery-motor-only spin with no independent mechanical input
measurement_gate.decisive_metric: Only count recovered electrical energy when its source is traceable to independently measured mechanical work or rotor kinetic-energy decrease.

copper_brass_implication.rule: Do not try to harvest the Axle's bulk eddy currents through solid copper/brass as the main generator architecture.
copper_brass_implication.reason: They form poorly controlled circulating currents, cause braking and heat, and are harder to route efficiently to the battery than stationary designed windings.
copper_brass_implication.preferred: Use brass-class structural material if it wins the eddy/corrosion A/B; use intentional copper windings where electrical collection is desired.
